Front: What is the core insight about DNNs and noisy labels?
Back: DNNs fit clean patterns first (low-complexity features) then memorize noise later (high-complexity patterns). This temporal separation enables small-loss selection, early stopping, and curriculum-based methods.

Front: What error rate is typical in real-world training annotations?
Back: 5-40% of real-world training annotations contain errors, and neural networks memorize these errors after initially learning clean patterns.

Front: What is the core architectural decision for handling noisy labels?
Back: Filtering (remove suspected noisy samples) vs. Correction (estimate true labels or modify the loss function to tolerate noise).

Front: When should you choose filtering for noisy labels?
Back: When data is abundant (>100K samples) and noise is random. Methods: Co-teaching, cleanlab/Confident Learning.

Front: When should you choose loss correction for noisy labels?
Back: When data is scarce or the noise transition matrix T is estimable. Methods: forward T-correction, symmetric losses.

Front: When should you choose a hybrid approach (DivideMix)?
Back: When noise rates exceed 40% and you need maximum accuracy.

Front: What is the noise transition matrix T?
Back: A K x K stochastic matrix where T[i][j] = P(noisy_label=j | true_label=i). It describes the probability of each class being flipped to another class.

Front: How is the noise transition matrix T used for loss correction?
Back: Multiplying T-inverse with the loss function yields an unbiased estimator of the clean-data risk: L_corrected = T^(-1) * L. Forward correction: CE(T * softmax(f(x)), y_noisy).

Front: What are anchor points in noise-rate estimation?
Back: Samples for which P(y_true=i|x) = 1 — they belong to class i with certainty. Given anchor points, T[i][j] = P(y_noisy=j | anchor_i) can be directly estimated.

Front: When does T-matrix loss correction fail?
Back: When noise is instance-dependent (T varies per sample rather than being class-conditional), or when T is poorly conditioned (near-singular, condition number > 10), amplifying estimation errors.

Front: What is Confident Learning (cleanlab)?
Back: A framework that uses out-of-fold predicted probabilities to estimate the joint distribution P(noisy_label, true_label), then identifies samples where the model's prediction confidently disagrees with the given label.

Front: What are the three steps of the cleanlab methodology?
Back: (1) Generate out-of-fold predicted probabilities via K-fold cross-validation. (2) Compute class-specific thresholds t_j. (3) Flag samples where predicted probability for another class k exceeds t_k.

Front: Why does Confident Learning use class-specific thresholds?
Back: A model might be 90% confident on dogs but only 60% on wolves. A global threshold would under-detect noise in low-confidence classes and over-detect in high-confidence ones.

Front: What did Northcutt et al. find when applying Confident Learning to popular benchmarks?
Back: They found 3.3% average label error rate across 10 benchmarks, including 6% errors in ImageNet validation set. Correcting these improved accuracy by up to 10% without architectural changes.

Front: What is Co-teaching?
Back: Two networks train simultaneously; each selects its smallest-loss samples and feeds them to the other for training, preventing both from converging to the same memorized errors.

Front: Why does Co-teaching use two networks instead of one selecting its own samples?
Back: Self-training creates confirmation bias — the network preferentially selects samples it already fits, including memorized noisy ones. Two independently initialized networks provide a form of peer review.

Front: How does the Co-teaching sample selection rate R(t) work?
Back: R(t) starts at 100% and decays to (1 - noise_rate) over T_k epochs, gradually filtering more aggressively as both networks improve their ability to distinguish clean from noisy samples.

Front: What is DivideMix?
Back: A method that fits a two-component beta mixture model to per-sample losses, divides data into labeled (clean) and unlabeled (noisy) sets, then applies MixMatch semi-supervised learning on both.

Front: What is DivideMix's key insight about noisy samples?
Back: Discarding noisy samples wastes information — those samples still contain valid input features even if labels are wrong. Treating them as unlabeled data recovers this information via semi-supervised learning.

Front: What accuracy does DivideMix achieve on CIFAR-10 with 90% symmetric noise?
Back: 96.1% — only 2% below clean-data performance.

Front: What is the failure mode of DivideMix under asymmetric noise?
Back: The BMM may fail to separate clean and noisy distributions when confusion occurs between semantically similar classes (e.g., cat/dog), as the loss distributions overlap more.

Front: What is the noise-tolerance condition for a loss function under symmetric noise?
Back: The sum of losses over all classes must be constant: sum_k L(f(x), k) = C. If satisfied, the minimizer of the noisy risk equals the minimizer of the clean risk.

Front: Does MAE (Mean Absolute Error) satisfy the noise-tolerance condition?
Back: Yes. sum_k MAE(f(x), k) = K - 1, which is constant. However, MAE converges very slowly because its gradients are constant regardless of prediction confidence.

Front: Why does MAE underperform CE on noisy data in practice despite theoretical guarantees?
Back: MAE's constant gradient magnitude treats a 99% confident correct prediction the same as a 51% confident one. It cannot upweight confident correct predictions, severely slowing learning of clean patterns.

Front: What is Generalized Cross Entropy (GCE)?
Back: L_GCE = (1 - f(x)_y^q) / q. At q=0 it reduces to CE (fast, not robust). At q=1 it reduces to MAE (robust, slow). Setting q=0.7 gives a practical compromise.

Front: What is Symmetric Cross Entropy (SCE)?
Back: SCE = CE + alpha * RCE (reverse cross entropy). Combines standard CE with a reverse CE term to achieve noise tolerance while maintaining reasonable convergence speed.

Front: What is Flooding regularization?
Back: A method that prevents training loss from going below a threshold b: L_flood = |L - b| + b. Keeps the model in a broad minimum that resists memorization without requiring noise rate estimation.

Front: How does Flooding work mechanically?
Back: When loss > b: gradient is unchanged (normal training). When loss < b: gradient is REVERSED, pushing loss back up. This creates a random walk around flat minima.

Front: What is the practical recommendation hierarchy for robust loss functions?
Back: (1) Default: SCE (handles up to 30% symmetric noise). (2) High noise >30%: GCE q=0.7. (3) Unknown noise: Flooding. (4) Asymmetric noise: Forward T-correction.

Front: What is AUM (Area Under the Margin)?
Back: AUM_i = (1/E) * sum_e [logit_correct(e) - max_other_logit(e)]. A training-free metric that ranks samples by mislabel likelihood based on margin stability during training.

Front: How do you distinguish hard examples from mislabeled examples using AUM?
Back: Hard examples have low but positive AUM (model eventually learns them). Mislabeled examples have negative AUM (correct-class logit consistently below top incorrect logit).

Front: What AUROC does AUM achieve for separating noisy from clean labels?
Back: >0.98 AUROC on CIFAR-10 with symmetric noise.

Front: What is curriculum learning in the context of noisy labels?
Back: Ordering training samples from easy to hard, which naturally prioritizes clean samples (easy to fit) before noisy ones (hard/impossible to fit), providing implicit noise robustness.

Front: What is the main failure mode of curriculum learning under noise?
Back: Hardness conflates two causes: genuine complexity and label corruption. Separating these requires a secondary signal like ensemble disagreement or cross-validation confidence.

Front: What empirical benefit does curriculum learning provide on noisy data?
Back: It achieves the performance of training on approximately 30% more data, because early emphasis on clean patterns creates a stronger feature extractor resistant to subsequent noise.

Front: What is the self-paced learning variant of curriculum learning?
Back: Jointly optimizes model parameters theta and sample weights v: min sum(v_i * L(x_i)) - lambda * sum(v_i). Closed-form: v_i = 1 if L(x_i) < lambda, else 0. Lambda increases each epoch.

Front: What is importance reweighting for noisy labels?
Back: Assigns each sample weight w = T^(-1) applied to the label distribution, such that weighted noisy-data risk equals clean-data risk in expectation.

Front: Why does importance reweighting fail at high noise rates?
Back: T^(-1) produces extreme weights (>10) that increase variance dramatically, making training unstable. Fix: clip weights to [0.1, 10] range, accepting small bias for variance reduction.

Front: How does the memorization gap manifest in training dynamics?
Back: Clean-sample loss continues decreasing while noisy-sample loss plateaus then decreases slowly. The divergence point indicates when the network transitions from learning to memorizing.

Front: What is the typical epoch progression of DNN learning under noise?
Back: Epochs 1-20: learns common clean patterns (small-loss = clean). Epochs 20-100: learns decision boundaries (AUM separates clean/noisy). Epochs 100+: memorizes individual noisy labels.

Front: What is the memorization index for a sample?
Back: memorization_index(x_i) = accuracy_with(x_i) - accuracy_without(x_i). High values mean the model's ability to classify that sample depends entirely on having memorized it.

Front: How do you build a data flywheel that handles noisy user feedback?
Back: Convert implicit signals to probabilistic labels, aggregate across users via beta-binomial models to reduce noise, apply Confident Learning on aggregated labels, train on confident subset.

Front: Why does noise decrease with user aggregation in a feedback flywheel?
Back: Noise decreases at O(1/sqrt(N)) for N independent users. Popular items get clean labels quickly while tail items remain noisy — creating a natural curriculum.

Front: What is the flywheel noise accumulation problem?
Back: Each iteration introduces model bias into feedback collection (exposure bias). Over K iterations: effective_noise(K) ~ noise_base + K * feedback_bias without intervention.

Front: How do you mitigate the flywheel noise accumulation problem?
Back: (1) Exploration injection: 5-10% random traffic. (2) Propensity scoring: weight by 1/P(exposure|model). (3) Periodic clean-data injection for recalibration.

Front: What is the condition number of T and why does it matter?
Back: kappa(T) = ||T|| * ||T^(-1)|| governs sensitivity of loss correction to T estimation errors. When kappa > 10, small T errors produce large risk bias — correction becomes unreliable.

Front: How does Confident Learning relate to the noise transition matrix T?
Back: The confident joint C[i][j] relates to T via: T[i][j] = C[i][j] / sum_j C[i][j]. This provides T estimation without requiring strict anchor point assumptions.

Front: What is the cost advantage of AUM over cross-validation for noise detection?
Back: AUM computes noise scores during a single training run vs 5x cost for K-fold Confident Learning. Saves approximately 80% of detection compute.

Front: What is the most impactful intervention for production noise-robust training?
Back: Not algorithmic sophistication but clean validation data. Even 500 verified-clean samples enable reliable noise detection calibration and unbiased evaluation.

Front: What is open-set noise?
Back: Samples from out-of-distribution classes mixed into training data that violate the closed-set assumption of most noise-handling methods.

Front: What did Wei et al. (2022) show about real-world annotation noise?
Back: Human annotation noise on CIFAR-10N is instance-dependent and far less uniform than synthetic benchmarks assume. Real noise depends on individual sample difficulty, not just class identity.

Front: Compare Co-teaching vs DivideMix: when to use each?
Back: Co-teaching: noise rate 20-50%, need simplicity, two GPUs available. DivideMix: noise rate >40%, want maximum accuracy, willing to accept complexity.

Front: What is the theoretical lower bound for CE loss under symmetric noise?
Back: accuracy_noisy >= accuracy_clean * (1 - noise_rate). The actual degradation is typically worse than this bound for untreated models.

Front: What scaling issue arises with Confident Learning at 10M+ samples?
Back: K-fold cross-validation becomes intractable. Transition to AUM-based ranking or importance reweighting with streaming estimation, or train on curated subsets identified by fast heuristics.

Front: How do you detect the transition point from learning to memorization?
Back: Track per-sample loss trajectories and fit a two-component mixture model at each epoch. The transition occurs when the lower component (clean) stabilizes while the upper component (noisy) begins decreasing.

Front: What is the production threshold for including feedback items in training?
Back: Only include items where credible interval width < 0.3 AND total feedback count > 10 interactions. This naturally creates a curriculum from high-traffic (clean) to tail (noisy).

Front: How do you prevent a noise detection model from being corrupted by noisy training data?
Back: Bootstrap confidence: train K detectors on K subsets, flag samples all K agree are noisy (high precision), route disagreement set to human review.
